subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@acmehealth.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-18T15:00:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Hi Sam / Jordan —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. I’ve included Rishi and Aditya for the technical deep-dive and migration planning.

Attendees:
- Sam Park (Acme Health, Product)
- Jordan Lee (Acme Health, Platform)
- Marissa Cole (Redwood, Sales)
- Rishi Malhotra (Redwood, Solutions)

Pain points and goals (as discussed):
- Vendor lock-in & contract risk: heavy reliance on OpenAI for chat + Anthropic for assistant flows, worried about pricing spikes and limited control.
- Cost: current spend is rising due to high per-token costs and long-context workloads. Target is to reduce inference spend ~40% without regressing quality.
- Latency & reliability: P95 latency above acceptable for search-augmented flows during peak, need predictable endpoint behavior.
- Data control & compliance: PHI-sensitive PII in prompts requires stronger audit logs and private deployment options.
- Feature parity: must retain function-calling / streaming / tool integration and embeddings compatibility for retrieval stacks.

Current stack (summary):
- OpenAI: chat completions, function calls, streaming (primary for customer-facing assistant)
- Anthropic: assistant flows for sensitive prompts (fallbacks)
- Vector DB: Pinecone for embeddings + similarity search
- Orchestration: internal SDK wraps current providers; some hard-coded prompt templates and post-processing heuristics

Success criteria for migration pilot (what Acme needs to see to proceed):
- Quality: model prompt outputs match or exceed baseline on your eval set (we’ll use the test queries you mentioned).
- Latency: P95 < 350ms for short-form assistant queries (target 200–250ms where possible).
- Cost: >=40% reduction in per-inference cost at pilot volumes.
- Compatibility: function-calling and streaming must work with minimal code changes (SDK adapter approach preferred).
- Compliance: option for Private deployment (VPC / customer-managed) and audit logging for PHI flows.

Suggested model shortlist (initial):
- Llama 2 (13B) — good instruction-following, widely supported runtimes
- Mistral Instruct (7B/Chat) — strong cost/quality tradeoff for instruction tasks
- Falcon 40B — high capacity for complex reasoning and few-shot cases
- RedPajama / Open weights (7B-13B) — for faster iterations and on-prem options

Compatibility needs & technical notes:
- Function calling: must preserve existing callback formats for your SDK — we’ll prototype an adapter layer.
- Tokenizer differences: we’ll validate embedding/semantic-search vector drift and provide quantization/FP16 guidance.
- KV cache & continuous batching: Rishi will evaluate if existing caching heuristics carry over to the chosen runtime.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with engineering (Rishi + Aditya) — schedule 60–90m this week to review test queries and runtime constraints.
2) Acme to share sample test set + 3 representative production prompts (attaching CSV stub).
3) Redwood to propose a 2-week pilot plan (SOW draft attached) with cost estimate and success metrics.
4) Follow-up: align on pilot start date (target by 07/27 if feasible).

Attachments: acme-test-queries.csv (sample), redwood-sow-draft-v1.pdf (draft SOW), migration-checklist.xlsx

If I missed anything or you want this captured differently, let me know and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll loop Rishi/Aditya to propose slots for the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Thanks Marissa — this is great and captures everything. A few quick clarifications:
- We can share a redacted test set (CSV) by EOD tomorrow — will include ~500 queries across customer support, billing, and clinical triage.
- Pilot timeline: 2-week pilot works; ideally start 2026-07-27 and run through 2026-08-10 so we can present results to leadership on 08/12.
- Compliance: PHI workflows need audit trails and a SOC2-ready deployment; will need Redwood’s Private deployment option for that scope.

I’m uploading the redacted test set to the shared Drive and will send the link. For the technical deep-dive, Jordan and I can join any slots Rishi proposes — prefer morning PST.

Cheers,
Sam

> Suggested model shortlist (initial):
> - Llama 2 (13B)
> - Mistral Instruct (7B/Chat)
> - Falcon 40B
> - RedPajama / Open weights (7B-13B)

Thanks — queued. A few technical items I want covered during the deep-dive so we scope the pilot correctly:
- Streaming & function-calling parity: we’ll prototype adapters but need sample function schemas and expected error handling semantics.
- Embedding drift: please confirm which embedding model you currently use (OpenAI ada/embedding-002 or similar) and provide a small sample so we can run vector-sim comparisons.
- Batch sizes & latency targets: we’ll simulate your qps profile. If you have 99th/95th percentile token lengths, share them.
- Quantization guidance: if we push 4-bit/8-bit quantized inference for cost, we’ll validate quality degradation on your eval set.

I’ll propose two slots for tomorrow morning PST. Aditya — can you prepare an outline for runtime options (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and rough cost delta estimates for the shortlist?

-rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
